body.p: By default, comes with Oxygen Security Manager. It replaces the Java Security Manager, which has been removed from recent Java versions and is no longer compatible with Web Author as of version 29.0. If you are upgrading from version 28.1 (or earlier) to version 29, see the dedicated topic: .

The Oxygen Security Manager is a security layer that acts as a safety net, helping to protect against malicious plugins and various attacks. It allows the minimal file access permissions that the application requires to function properly:
READ access to the directory where the is deployed.
READ and WRITE access to the application's working directory.
READ and WRITE access to the temporary directory of the JVM (Java Virtual Machine).

section.title: Disabling Oxygen Security Manager
section.p: We do not recommend disabling the Oxygen Security Manager. However, in some specific use cases, you might need to disable it (for example, when developing a custom plugin). In production, we recommend keeping the Oxygen Security Manager enabled, as it is an important security layer of the application.

p.note: You might also have to disable the Java Security Manager by removing the -Djava.security.manager option, if it is present.

section.p: To disable the default security mode, follow the procedure for your installation method:

ol.li: Go to the installation directory of .
In the Java Options section, declare the -Dcom.oxygenxml.disable.security=true system property.

section.title: Configuring Oxygen Security Manager for the Web Author Component WAR Distribution
section.p: The Oxygen Security Manager is enabled by default. However, integrators who use the WAR kit from Oxygen XML Web Author Component (not the regular Oxygen XML Web Author Linux and Windows installers or the All Platforms kit) need to configure it so that the application starts successfully. To do this, follow these steps:

ol.li: Specify the location of the oxygen.policy file using the -Doxygen.security.policy system property. The Oxygen Security Manager requires an oxygen.policy file that specifies permissions. You can obtain this file from the All Platforms kit. If you previously had additional permissions in catalina.policy, you must now add them to oxygen.policy.The oxygen.policy uses internal classes from the ro.sync.security package. It does not use JRE permission classes that are deprecated for removal and are not supported.

Add the -javaagent:./tomcat/webapps/oxygen-xml-web-author/WEB-INF/lib/oxygen-sandbox.jar JVM argument. Before starting Tomcat, make sure that the application is deployed at the oxygen-xml-web-author path and that the WAR file is expanded (unzipped). Otherwise, the javaagent JAR location will not exist on disk.

ul.li: XML External Entities that reference files inside JAR archives are not allowed.

section.title: Configuring File Permissions to Custom Locations
section.p: In some cases, needs to access file system resources, but for security reasons, you want to prevent your users from opening them directly in the editing page using the file:// protocol.

section.title: Security Options
section.p: comes with several security options preconfigured, which may prevent some documents from loading (for example, in development mode). These options are:

ul.li: ignore.absolute.file.system.entities - If set to true (default value), system entities with an absolute URL (file://URL) are ignored.
ignore.extenal.entities.outside.frameworks - If set to true (default value), XML external entities are resolved only if their target is inside a framework folder in the DITA-OT folder.

block.cross.protocol.system.entities - If set to true (default value), XML external entities are blocked if their target URL does not have the same protocol as the URL of the file where the entity is declared.

block.cross.protocol.author.references - If set to true (default value), Author references (for example, DITA conref) are blocked if their target URL has a different protocol than the URL of the file that contains the referencing element.
author.display.references.expanded - If set to false, referenced content is not expanded and displayed in the visual editor.

section.note: XML external entities that use URLs with the jar protocol are blocked unless the XML file that declares the entity is loaded from a URL that uses the jar protocol.
